title: Biocontainment Transport of High-Consequence Infectious Disease Patients: An Integrated Operational Model for Emergency Medical Systems
content:
Background/Objectives: Transport of patients with high-consequence infectious diseases (HCID) constitutes a critical interface between biosafety and emergency medicine. While biosafety frameworks originated in laboratory settings, their translation to mobile emergency systems introduces unique clinical, organisational, and human-factor chal-lenges. This paper describes and analyses an integrated operational model for biocon-tainment transport within emergency medical systems, addressing its theoretical foun-dations, procedural architecture, team governance structure, and determinants of safety and resilience.
Methods: An integrated systemic model of biocontainment transport is presented, in-corporating biosafety classification principles, operational protocols, device performance monitoring, governance frameworks, and human-factor considerations.
Results: The model rests on four interdependent pillars: personal protective equipment (PPE), physical containment envelope, negative pressure with HEPA filtration, and structured decontamination. Operational safety relies on structured pre-transport as-sessment, systematic device verification, complexity-based team composition, and a re-sponsibility allocation matrix. Continuous monitoring of environmental parameters and procedural compliance is expected to enhance system reliability. Psychological impact on both patients and operators emerged as a significant determinant of system sustainability. Model application across 1,585 transports yielded a zero operator contagion rate and no significant technical interruptions or containment chain failures.
Conclusions: Biocontainment transport should be conceptualised as an integrated emergency system rather than a device-centred intervention. Governance clarity, scalability, continuous skill maintenance, and human-factor integration are critical components for resilient HCID transport within emergency care systems.
